static.html:
Song of the Wild Earth

The morning wind hums softly through the pines, and the river answers in a silver refrain. This is a song for nature—for forests, waters, sunlight, and the quiet wonder of the living world.

Verse One

The dawn wakes up in the branches,
With a golden hand on the leaves;
The meadow sways in hush and shimmer,
And the whole wide world breathes.

static.html:
Verse Two

The mountains keep their patient silence,
While birds sketch songs across the sky;
Each root, each stone, each drifting cloudscape
Knows the reason why.

We walk among the wild and growing,
And the earth returns our care;
In every branch and blade and shadow,
There is a promise there.

static.html:
Verse Three

So let us sing for the cedar,
For the tide, the bloom, the rain;
For the hush of dawn in woodland valleys,
For the healing of the plain.

Nature is the first great chorus,
And we are but a note inside;
When we honor the green and glorious,
We let the whole world glide.

Let the earth keep singing through us.
